conflicts.resolution: Treat every oracle address as a discovery candidate; use the ABI pattern only for local mocks until the shared identity gate passes.
conflicts.subject: Oracle address and interface identity
conflicts.summary: Official pages publish asset-to-address mappings and AggregatorV3 examples, but no reviewed chain observation or issuer-to-bytecode correlation is present in this release.

conflicts.resolution: Treat WUSDC as the implementation-level input/output required by the reviewed SDK; do not equate WUSDC with native Circle USDC or claim reserve quality beyond issuer documentation.
conflicts.subject: QUSDC backing asset terminology
conflicts.summary: QUSDC product pages often say USDC generically, while the detailed flow and SDK use WUSDC as the QIE-side input and redemption asset.

conflicts.resolution: Retain the address as a lending configuration candidate only; do not label it as the QUSDC token, WUSDC token or vault without issuer and ABI identity evidence.
conflicts.subject: QUSDC address role in the lending SDK
conflicts.summary: The lending SDK publishes 0x3F43... as the QUSDC market underlying, while the QUSDC SDK requires separate vaultAddress and wusdcAddress constructor inputs and publishes no deployment address.

domains.title: Transactions and gas

integrations.description: Compound-style lending interface described by the official QIE Lending SDK with comptroller and cToken market roles.

interfaces.description: cToken function fragments shipped in the pinned SDK ABI.
interfaces.name: mint(uint256), borrow(uint256), repayBorrow(uint256), redeemUnderlying(uint256)

interfaces.description: Comptroller fragments used for borrow preparation and portfolio health display.
interfaces.name: enterMarkets(address[]) and getAccountLiquidity(address)

known_limitations: Published addresses and ABI fragments are discovery evidence, not proof of current deployed compatibility.
Borrow and collateral safety requires live market metadata and oracle evidence not supplied by the SDK.
No npm registry publication was found; the README instructs GitHub installation.

inputs: Market key and raw BigInt underlying amount
Underlying token and cToken candidate identities
Signer with allowance and balance
limitations: SDK calls approveIfNeeded and then cToken.mint without a configured receipt wait in supply.js.
Market and token addresses are published candidates, not identity-approved deployments.
Amount decimals are caller-configured in config.js and are not read dynamically.
operations.name: Supply an underlying asset

inputs: Market key and raw BigInt borrow amount
Signer, comptroller candidate and cToken candidate
limitations: The SDK enters the market as a state-changing side effect before borrow simulation.
borrow.js does not guard an unknown market before dereferencing its cToken.
Liquidity, collateral factors, oracle values, caps and liquidation parameters are not read by the SDK.
operations.name: Borrow a market asset
outputs: enterMarkets receipt followed by cToken.borrow transaction object

inputs: Market key and raw BigInt amount
Underlying token approval and signer
limitations: repay.js approves every time and does not wait for or validate a receipt after repayBorrow.
No max-repay or balance normalization is implemented.
operations.name: Repay a loan

inputs: Market key and raw BigInt underlying amount
Signer and cToken candidate
limitations: No local simulation, allowance check or receipt wait is performed by withdraw.js.
Cash and liquidity constraints are not checked before the write.
operations.name: Withdraw supplied underlying

inputs: Read-only provider, user address and configured market candidates
limitations: balanceOfUnderlying is marked nonpayable in the shipped ABI but called with staticCall.
Health divides a raw liquidity value by 1e18 without documenting the protocol's exact price/scale semantics.
A nonzero shortfall is reduced to health 0 and comptroller error codes are not surfaced.
operations.name: Read user portfolio
outputs: supplied and borrowed raw amounts plus a numeric health value

inputs: Read-only provider and configured market candidates
limitations: Totals sum cToken totalSupply values across markets with different decimals and do not normalize to a common denomination.
No market metadata freshness or deployment identity check is included.
operations.name: Read protocol totals
outputs: Decimal-string totalSupply and totalBorrow sums across configured markets

unresolved_questions: Which deployment, implementation and proxy addresses are current on QIE Mainnet?
What are the live collateral factors, liquidation thresholds, caps, rates and oracle sources?
Does the deployed ABI match the shipped minimal JSON fragments?

integrations.description: Officially documented asset feed product with a published mapping table and AggregatorV3-style read examples.

interfaces.description: Source-documented read interface for price and round metadata.
interfaces.name: latestRoundData(), getRoundData(uint80), decimals()

known_limitations: Official docs describe AggregatorV3 compatibility but no QIE runtime call or ABI/bytecode match was executed.
Aggregation and manipulation-resistance statements are issuer documentation, not an independent audit.

inputs: Issuer-authenticated feed address
Read-only provider
limitations: Feed addresses in the official mapping remain candidates until the shared identity gate passes.
Price scale must be read from decimals and checked against the feed's documented base/quote.
updatedAt freshness and positive-range checks are application responsibilities.
operations.name: Read latestRoundData
outputs: roundId, signed answer, startedAt, updatedAt and answeredInRound

unresolved_questions: Are all mapped feed contracts current and issuer-owned on QIE Mainnet?
What update interval and outage fallback policy applies to each feed?

integrations.description: Issuer-documented QIE receipt-token protocol whose detailed flow uses WUSDC as the QIE-side backing asset and QUSDC as the receipt asset.

interfaces.description: Minimal vault ABI fragment used by the official JavaScript SDK.
interfaces.name: depositAndMint(uint256) / burnAndWithdraw(uint256)

interfaces.description: ERC-20 methods the SDK uses to prepare WUSDC allowance and parse human-readable amounts.
interfaces.name: ERC-20 allowance, approve and decimals

known_limitations: Issuer documentation uses both generic USDC language and the more specific WUSDC implementation flow.
The official SDK contains no deployment address and no reserve-proof or upgrade-authority inspection.
1:1 receipt semantics are issuer-documented claims, not an independently verified market-price guarantee.

inputs: Human-readable WUSDC amount or raw integer amount
Approved vault and WUSDC identities
Signer-controlled account with sufficient WUSDC and gas
limitations: SDK requires separate vaultAddress and wusdcAddress inputs.
Production vault, WUSDC and QUSDC identities are not issuer-authenticated in this release.
A receipt is not proof of minting, reserve backing or economic value.
operations.name: Mint QUSDC from WUSDC
outputs: QUSDC balance change only after application-specific verification

inputs: Human-readable amount or raw integer amount in the SDK's WUSDC-derived scale
QUSDC balance and the reviewed vault identity
Signer-controlled account with sufficient QUSDC and gas
limitations: The SDK uses the WUSDC decimals lookup for both mint and burn parsing; QUSDC decimal equality is not independently established.
Redemption availability, fees, pause controls and reserve liquidity are not verified on a deployment.
Bridging WUSDC back to Ethereum is a separate cross-chain operation.
operations.name: Redeem QUSDC to WUSDC
outputs: WUSDC balance change only after application-specific verification

inputs: WUSDC candidate address and read-only provider
limitations: A contract-returned decimals value is observation metadata, not proof of token identity or economic denomination.
Do not default to 6 or 18 without the selected token's read result.
operations.name: Read WUSDC decimals
outputs: uint8 decimals value returned by the token contract

unresolved_questions: Which exact QIE contracts are the current production QUSDC token, WUSDC token and vault on each network?
Are minting, redemption, pause, fee and upgrade controls present in the deployed bytecode?
What independent reserve or supply reconciliation evidence is currently published?
